class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10"><b class="ssrcss-1xjjfut-BoldText e5tfeyi3">A woman who endured years of abusive controlling behaviour by her ex-husband says it has cost her more than £105,000 to divorce him.</b></p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Annabelle Boucher, 48, from Somerset, wants the law changed after she paid £75,000 to David Rogers, 61, despite him admitting to coercive and controlling behaviour. She also had to pay her legal costs.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"I thought being stuck in this relationship I couldn't get out of would be highlighted within the divorce procedure," Boucher said. "But the divorce law doesn't take into account the fact that he was a criminal."</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it had begun a consultation to reform the law so "family courts meet the needs of domestic abuse victims".</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Boucher, a mother from Chiselborough, said Rogers had come into her life in "a whirlwind" in 2017 and the pair got married two years later.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">It was once they were married that things started to "take a turn", she said, and "some very extreme behaviour started to happen". </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"It creeps up on you and you're in it, and so you don't kind of notice what is happening."</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Boucher said she had ended up "shutting down emotionally" and "cutting off from everyone" because she feared what would happen.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"You find that you're trapped within a situation that you can't get out of."</p></div></div></div></div><div data-block="image" data-testid="rich-text"><div class="ssrcss-nqezkk-RichTextContainer e5tfeyi1"><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The abuse was reported to police and Rogers was arrested on 24 February 2024.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">The divorce was finalised in September 2025 while criminal proceedings were ongoing. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">In April 2026, Rogers pleaded guilty to coercive and controlling behaviour at Taunton Crown Court and was given a 20-month suspended prison sentence.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Boucher said she knew there was going to be a financial split with the divorce, but added she had always kept her family home and Rogers had kept his. They had also paid bills separately. </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">She ended up paying Rogers a lump sum of £75,000 and more than £30,000 in her own legal costs.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"I cannot believe, in this day and age, in 2025, when my divorce was finalised, [criminal proceedings] do not have any implication at all," she added.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Boucher said she had had to take out personal loans to cover the costs, which had been "crippling".</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"I should be paying off these figures for years to come, so I'm not going to be free of this situation for several years."</p></div></div></div></div><div data-block="media" just think it's very sad that people that have been through far worse than this are still told that that has no relevance to the divorce proceedings they're going through, and I just think it's even further punishment for the victim."</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Olive Craig, senior legal officer for Rights of Women, a charity campaigning for the legal rights and safety of women, said divorce courts refused to really consider domestic abuse unless it passed "a very high threshold". </p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"You're more likely to get a family court judge to take physical violence into account, but coercive control is often very insidious behaviour," she said.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"It's often much more manipulative behaviour and family court judges, even within the legal framework, are effectively being told that they should consider that as irrelevant to the financial decisions that they make."</p><div class="ssrcss-2st5ed-ListContainer e5tfeyi0"><ul role="list"><li><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10"><i class="ssrcss-xbdn93-ItalicText e5tfeyi2">If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at </i><a href="/actionline" class="ssrcss-1e0jzsh-InlineLink e1kn3p7n0"><i class="ssrcss-xbdn93-ItalicText e5tfeyi2">BBC Action Line</i></a></p></li></ul></div><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">Kit O'Brien, a family law specialist based in Taunton, said there was now a "massively changed recognition of the effect domestic violence can have during a relationship", but things still needed to change.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">"The changes that are being talked about are not going to mean that every incidence of bad behaviour is going to suddenly change the way that finances are resolved," she said.</p><p class="ssrcss-1q0x1qg-Paragraph e1jhz7w10">But she said it could mean "it's going https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c70l.visible_text: Somerset woman's divorce from abusive husband cost her £105k - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World Asia UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat England Regions Somerset Divorcing abusive husband cost woman £105k Image caption, Annabelle Boucher says coercive control needs to be considered by family courts when divorce settlements are reached By Laura Jones , Beth Cruse , West of England and Rachel Andrews , Somerset Published 9 September 2026 A woman who endured years of abusive controlling behaviour by her ex-husband says it has cost her more than £105,000 to divorce him. Annabelle Boucher, 48, from Somerset, wants the law changed after she paid £75,000 to David Rogers, 61, despite him admitting to coercive and controlling behaviour. She also had to pay her legal costs. "I thought being stuck in this relationship I couldn't get out of would be highlighted within the divorce procedure," Boucher said. "But the divorce law doesn't take into account the fact that he was a criminal." The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it had begun a consultation to reform the law so "family courts meet the needs of domestic abuse victims". Boucher, a mother from Chiselborough, said Rogers had come into her life in "a whirlwind" in 2017 and the pair got married two years later. It was once they were married that things started to "take a turn", she said, and "some very extreme behaviour started to happen". "It creeps up on you and you're in it, and so you don't kind of notice what is happening." Boucher said she had ended up "shutting down emotionally" and "cutting off from everyone" because she feared what would happen. "You find that you're trapped within a situation that you can't get out of." Image source, Avon and Somerset Police Image caption, David Rogers, from Norton-sub-Hamdon, in Somerset, pleaded guilty to controlling and coercive behaviour in April The abuse was reported to police and Rogers was arrested on 24 February 2024. The divorce was finalised in September 2025 while criminal proceedings were ongoing. In April 2026, Rogers pleaded guilty to coercive and controlling behaviour at Taunton Crown Court and was given a 20-month suspended prison sentence. Boucher said she knew there was going to be a financial split with the divorce, but added she had always kept her family home and Rogers had kept his. They had also paid bills separately. She ended up paying Rogers a lump sum of £75,000 and more than £30,000 in her own legal costs. "I cannot believe, in this day and age, in 2025, when my divorce was finalised, [criminal proceedings] do not have any implication at all," she added. Boucher said she had had to take out personal loans to cover the costs, which had been "crippling". "I should be paying off these figures for years to come, so I'm not going to be free of this situation for several years." Figure caption, Boucher said the law needed to "catch up with the times of now", adding: "I just think it's very sad that people that have been through far worse than this are still told that that has no relevance to the divorce proceedings they're going through, and I just think it's even further punishment for the victim." Olive Craig, senior legal officer for Rights of Women, a charity campaigning for the legal rights and safety of women, said divorce courts refused to really consider domestic abuse unless it passed "a very high threshold". "You're more likely to get a family court judge to take physical violence into account, but coercive control is often very insidious behaviour," she said. "It's often much more manipulative behaviour and family court judges, even within the legal framework, are effectively being told that they should consider that as irrelevant to the financial decisions that they make." If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line Kit O'Brien, a family law specialist based in Taunton, said there was now a "massively changed recognition of the effect domestic violence can have during a relationship", but things still needed to change. "The changes that are being talked about are not going to mean that every incidence of bad behaviour is going to suddenly change the way that finances are resolved," she said. But she said it could mean "it's going to be approached in a way that is rather more reflective of society as it is now". Image caption, Kit O'Brien from Walker Family Law says there was more recognition in courts of the effect of domestic violence in a relationship, but further change was needed An MoJ spokesperson said: "We recognise the devastating impact domestic abuse, including economic abuse and coercive control, has on victims during and after a relationship." The MoJ added it would consider all the responses to its consultation carefully "before finalising policy." Craig said she was "really pleased" the government was looking at options about the way domestic abuse should be considered in financial remedy proceedings. She added: "It should reflect the very real economic consequences of abuse and also prevent perpetrators from benefiting from their own abusive conduct."     <div id="block-receptionfaqblockdab">
  
      <h2>DAB FAQs</h2>
    
      <div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Why am I unable to receive Local Radio, or National Radio such as BBC Radio Scotland, on my DAB Radio?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<p><span>The BBC's local and national radio services are carried on local commercial DAB Multiplexes. Please see our help page to see </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/dab-radio/what-is-a-dab-multiplex"><span><strong><u>how DAB multiplexes work</u></strong></span></a><span>, Therefore, you may not be receiving this service, as there is not a commercial DAB service in your local area. To check what coverage of DAB services are available</span> <span>in your locality, please see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults"><span><strong><u> Transmitter checker tool</u></strong></span></a><span>.</span></p>
</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">My DAB reception has started to drop out, is this due to poor reception?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<p><span>Firstly, poor reception might be down to poor coverage, so it is best to check you are in a DAB coverage area. Use our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults"><span><strong><u>transmitter tool</u></strong></span></a><span>, which will tell you what national and local DAB services are available in your locality.</span></p><p><span>Secondly, If you are in a good coverage area, and are still receiving poor DAB reception </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/problem-assistant"><span><strong><u>please try our Problem Assistant</u></strong></span></a><span> for further advice.</span></p><p> </p>
</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">How can weather affect DAB reception?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<p ><span ><span ><span ><span >DAB reception is rarely disrupted by high-pressure weather conditions, but under some circumstances, signals from very distant transmitters can cause reception to break up, or be lost for periods of time. If you suspect this - particularly if you are also getting interference on FM - wait until the weather changes.</span></span></span> </span></p>



</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Can LED Lights Interfere with my DAB Reception?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<p><span ><span ><span ><span >There is a possibility some LED Lights can cause interference to DAB and FM Radio Reception, particularly if LED lights are used to replace halogen lights, and retain the original transformer.  This is because the power used is lower, and is forced to work outside of its normal operating parameters, resulting in electrical impulse interference. For more information on interference, please see our </span></span></span></span><a href="https://www.radioandtvhelp.co.uk/"><b><u><span ><span ><span >RTIS site</span></span></span></u></b></a></p>



</div></div><hr>

  </div>
<div id="block-receptionsimplecheckdab">
  
      <h2>DAB Help Guides</h2>
    
      <div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">What is a good DAB installation?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<hr><blockquote><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Coverage and location</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Your radio must be in a good DAB coverage area to receive BBC services. Have a look at our </span><a href="/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Transmitter Checker</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"><strong> </strong>to see what BBC services you can receive where you are.<strong> </strong>If you live in a basement flat, or your building is steel-framed or reinforced concrete, coverage may be affected.  </span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Tuning</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Most DAB radios can be tuned easily at the touch of a button. Sometimes a full scan is required. Portable radios should be tuned in a location in your home where the best possible signal is received. Most DAB radios come with built in signal strength meters which can be helpful.  From time to time radios should be re-tuned in order to discover new stations.   </span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>Telescopic aerials</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-AU">Telescopic aerials on portable radios should be fully extended to receive a good signal.  Tilting and swivelling the aerial will help to get the best signal.  Broken aerials may affect reception.    </span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>Outdoor aerials</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-AU">An externally mounted aerial can be attached to many types of DAB portable radio and hi-fi systems. DAB aerials are different from FM or TV aerials, so you need a good quality DAB-specific aerial.  An indoor aerial may be good enough, but for the best reception use an outdoor one. Ideally, this should be on the roof or high up on the outside of the building, though it may also give good results in the loft.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>Cables and Connectors</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-AU">If you have an external aerial, a radio signal will always lose some of its strength as it passes along the cable and through the connectors. It is important to minimise the loss by using good quality cable and connectors.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>DAB radio in cars</strong></span></em></p><p>DAB uses different frequencies from FM radio. We advise you check that your antenna is able to receive DAB, in the majority of cases you will need a new antenna. An exception is "helically wound" FM aerials. <a href="/reception/help-guides/dab-radio/dab-radio-in-the-car"><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>See our guide on DAB radio in cars</strong></span></a></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Qualified Installer</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The BBC cannot recommend individual Installers. </span><a href="https://www.getmeviewing.org.uk/"><strong>GetMeViewing</strong></a> is the consumer site for CAI Ltd (Confederation of Aerial Industries) which <span lang="EN-US">is a recognised trade body which will put you in touch with one of their members in your area.</span></p></blockquote>
</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Troubleshooting DAB reception
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<hr><blockquote><p> </p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Transmitter faults</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">By using our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults/#/undefined"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Transmitter Checker</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US">, you can check which DAB radio services are available at your location. It will also show you any transmitter faults. Currently it reports on network DAB stations only; Local and Nations radio faults are not included.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Works and Warnings</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Check whether there are any known </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/works-warnings"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>works or warnings</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"> that might be causing the problem.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Tuning</strong> </span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">DAB uses multiplexes to group services together. The BBC network stations, e.g. BBC Radio 1, BBC Radio 4 are grouped together in a single multiplex. Nations and Local radio services are carried on a mix of commercial multiplexes.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Try switching your radio on and off. If you still have a problem use the ‘autotune' function to re-tune. If this does not work, a full re-scan might be needed. Check your radio manual for specific instructions on doing a full re-scan. Further information on tuning your DAB radio can be found by visiting the </span><a href="https://getdigitalradio.com/your-stations/retune/"><span lang="EN-US">Get Digital</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> site or see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/dab-radio/dab-tuning-information"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>DAB tuning guide</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"><strong>.</strong></span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Portable Radios</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Ensure the telescopic/integrated aerial is fully extended. Try moving the radio around to see if you can find a better position where you get good reception of all the stations you want to listen to.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">In most circumstances the supplied telescopic aerial should be perfectly adequate, and as a rule of thumb DAB aerials tend to work best when vertical and extended at least 35 cm. If your radio reception is poor then you could consider an external aerial for best reception quality. Even in good areas an external aerial will guarantee optimum performance and will also ensure consistent listening quality.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Many Digital radios have a signal strength display which enables you to position the Radio for the best reception (usually a number of blocks) as a guide of reception quality. Unfortunately, some radios are less sensitive than others and need careful positioning to work reliably. If your radio displays signal strength, use this as a guide to ensure the best position.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/dab-radio/what-is-a-good-dab-installation"><span lang="EN-US">DAB installation guide</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> provides further information.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>External aerials</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">It is important to check the cables and the aerial for damage and that they are operating correctly. Make sure any cables between your radio equipment and aerial are connected securely. For further information see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/dab-radio/what-is-a-good-dab-installation"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>DAB installation guide</strong>.</span></a></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Damaged Cables</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Water can get into external cables and can cause reception problems. To rule this out see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/everything-else/water-ingress"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>guide on water damage to cables</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US">.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Car Radios</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Radio reception can drop out when on the move due to changes in topography. See our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/dab-radio/dab-radio-in-the-car"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>car radio guide</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"><strong> </strong>for more information.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Weather</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Radio signals can be affected by fine weather including high pressure. The only solution is to wait for the weather to change, you should not re-tune during this time. Our information on h</span>ow clear skies and fine weather can affect your radio reception <span lang="EN-US">may be useful, please see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/fmmwlw-radio/radio-reception-problems-due-to-high-pressure"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>weather guide.</strong></span></a></p><p><em><strong>Lost reception of one or more station within a multiplex</strong></em></p><p>If all other stations are working ok and you have just lost one station. The problem could be due to a number of reasons, the station may have stopped broadcasting or have moved multiplexes rather than a radio fault. All of the stations in one multiplex should be behaving the same way. </p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Interference</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">If you are still having problems, it is possible an unwanted signal is the cause. For information on the </span><a href="https://www.radioandtvhelp.co.uk/"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>symptoms of interference see our sister website RTIS</strong></span></a><a href="https://www.radioandtvhelp.co.uk/interference"><span lang="EN-US"> </span></a><span lang="EN-US">.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Qualified Installer</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The BBC cannot recommend individual installers. The </span><a href="https://www.cai.org.uk/"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>CAI (</strong></span></a><a href="https://www.getmeviewing.org.uk/"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Confederation of Aerial Industries</strong></span></a><a href="https://www.cai.org.uk/"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>)</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"> is a recognised trade body which will be able to put you in touch with one of their members in your area.</span></p></blockquote><p> </p>
</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">DAB radio in the car
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<hr />
<blockquote>
<p> </p>

<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">To listen to DAB in your car you will need to ensure your aerial is able to receive a DAB signal. You may need to contact your car manufacturer to check. However, helically wound FM aerials are able to receive DAB.</span></span></span></p>

<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">The best place to put a DAB aerial is on the roof of the car and as far from the engine as possible, to avoid any interference.</span></span></span></p>
</blockquote>

<p> </p>

<blockquote>
<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">If your car radio is showing no signal or no service for a station you usually receive, this could be down to one of the following things:</span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><strong>DAB Transmitter Fault</strong></span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">If you know your location, you can use our <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults/#/undefined"><strong>transmitter checker</strong></a> to see whether there is a problem. If not, then check the radio and the aerial to confirm they are working correctly.</span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span><span><strong><span lang="EN-US">Interference</span></strong> </span></span></em></p>

<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">Poor DAB reception can also be caused by equipment used in the vehicle. For example, phone chargers or dash cams sometimes cause interference and affect your radio signal. Try unplugging the items to see if one of them is causing any interference.</span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span><span><strong><span lang="EN-US">Retuning & DAB Pre-set Stations</span></strong></span></span></em></p>

<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">If you have bought a new car, the DAB radio may be tuned to DAB stations in a different location. Delete the presets and re-tune to the services in your area.</span></span></span></p>

<p><em><strong>Topography</strong></em></p>

<p><span><span><span lang="EN-US">When travelling in the car, your signal can be affected by </span></span></span>natural features of the land, for example, hills, valleys, rivers, etc. The signal should return once you move away from these features.</p>
</blockquote>

</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Part time/secondary radio services on DAB
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<blockquote>
<hr />
<p> </p>

<p><em><strong><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span>Where can I find them?</span></span></span></strong><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span> </span></span></span></em></p>
</blockquote>

<blockquote>
<p><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span>When Radio 5 Sports Extra is on air, you should find it right next to 5 Live on the list of stations on your digital radio.</span></span></span><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span> </span></span></span></p>

<p><em><strong><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span>When do they broadcast?</span></span></span></strong></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span>Radio 5 Sports Extra has a dynamic schedule. To see what is available when, the BBC keeps a schedule on the <strong><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/5livesportsextra">sport website</a></strong>. </span></span></span></p>

<p>A marketing audio loop plays before and after the scheduled programmes.</p>

<p><em><strong><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span>How to find these services</span></span></span></strong></em><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span> </span></span></span></p>

<p><span lang="EN-AU"><span><span>It is best to re-tune your radio when they are broadcasting, so it will store the station in its memory.</span></span></span></p>
</blockquote>

</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Who is responsible for my Shared/Communal Aerial?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<hr><blockquote><p><span lang="EN-AU">It is worth first checking to see whether the problem is with your own equipment, or the local transmitter. If neighbours are having the same problem it may be that the aerial itself is at fault, or there may be an interfering signal. In either case, you will need to ask your landlord or management committee to solve the problem.</span></p><p> </p><p><em><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>Checking for problems</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Check cables and leads within your property to ensure the problem is not a simple installation fault. Please see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview-freely/what-is-a-good-freeview-installation"><span lang="EN-US">Freeview Installation guide</span></a><a href="/reception/help-guides/freeview/what-is-a-good-freeview-installation"><span lang="EN-US"> </span></a><span lang="EN-US">for further details. </span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">To see whether there are any faults with the local transmitters use our </span><a href="/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults/"><span lang="EN-US">Transmitter Checker tool.</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> This will help you to see if there are, or have been recently, transmitter faults in your local area. </span></p><p> </p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Electrical interference</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">There are differences between a reception problem and one caused by electrical interference. See our </span><a href="/reception/help-guides"><span lang="EN-US">help guides</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> which explain the differences. Our sister site, the </span><a href="https://www.radioandtvhelp.co.uk/"><span lang="EN-US">Radio and Television Investigation Service (RTIS)</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> also has useful information on how to distinguish the difference.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">If it is potentially interference, your landlord or management committee can contact the regulator, Ofcom, for help with solving the problem, </span><a href="https://www.ofcom.org.uk/make-a-complaint/complain-about-wireless-interference/interference-to-tv-and-radio-services"><span lang="EN-US">using their contact web form</span></a><a href="https://www.ofcom.org.uk/complaints/complain-about-wireless-interference/interference-to-wireless-devices-at-home/interference-to-tv-and-radio-services"><span lang="EN-US">.</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> Since it is a communal aerial, you will not be able to contact Ofcom directly.</span></p></blockquote><blockquote><p> </p><p> </p></blockquote>
</div></div><hr>

  </div>

<div id="block-advancedchecks">
  
      <h2>Freeview Help Guides</h2>
    
      <div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">What is a good Freeview installation?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<hr><blockquote><p> </p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Aerials</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">There are all kinds of aerials available on the market and some which are specific to certain frequencies. A wideband aerial is a popular choice, although there are other aerials available. A qualified aerial installer with local knowledge will be able to advise further.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Height</strong> </span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Your aerial should be as high as possible pointing towards the transmitter with the best signal. Use the our </span><a href="/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults/" target="_blank"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Transmitter Checker</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"><strong> </strong>tool to determine the best transmitter for your location. Ensure there is nothing in front of the aerial that could block the signal, such as trees. All TV reception predictions assume an outside aerial at a height of 10m from the ground.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Loft and indoor aerials</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">If you live close to a transmitter or can get a strong TV signal, then it could be possible to use an aerial in your loft or an indoor portable aerial. However, in both cases the signal will be weakened as it has to pass through various obstructions such as walls, roof tiles, foil backed insulation etc. Even if you are predicted to have good reception, you may have problems receiving services using indoor or loft aerials.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Cable and connectors</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">A television signal will always lose some of its strength as it passes along the cable and through the connectors. Therefore it is important to minimise the loss by using good quality cable and connectors.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Amplifier</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">These are not recommended unless absolutely required as they can introduce unexpected reception problems. See our </span><a href="/reception/help-guides/freeview/how-to-choose-the-right-amplifier"><span lang="EN-US"><strong>help guide on the different types of amplifiers available</strong></span></a><span lang="EN-US"><strong>. </strong></span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Polarisation</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Depending on the transmitter you are using, your aerial elements will need to be mounted flat (horizontal) or on its side (vertical). A qualified aerial installer with local knowledge will be able to advise further.</span></p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Qualified Installer</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">We cannot recommend individual installers. However </span><a href="https://www.getmeviewing.org.uk/"><strong>GetMeViewing</strong></a> is the consumer site for CAI Ltd (Confederation of Aerial Industries) which<span lang="EN-US"> is a recognised trade body which will be able to put you in touch with one of their members in your area.</span></p><p> </p></blockquote><hr><p> </p>
</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Troubleshooting your Freeview Television reception
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<blockquote><p>Effects of poor Freeview reception are: </p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ebd536b8c2307285ffd9b51fdaa44725c">loss of channels</li><li data-list-item-id="e0b48bbbf8b9f5e79d264540cb3b898bb">picture break up</li><li data-list-item-id="e438c814b72c813e228a01d8fc944e211">sound glitches/break up  </li></ul><p><br><strong>Step 1 – Check if there is a fault with your local transmitter </strong><br><br>First, use our <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults">Transmitter Checker</a> tool. If there is a fault, it will be highlighted.  If there is more than one transmitter listed, check all of them.  </p><p>If there is no problem with the transmitter, visit our <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/works-warnings">Works & Warnings page</a>. We advise of known issues, major transmitter work and whether <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview-freely/how-clear-skies-and-fine-weather-can-affect-your-tv-reception">high pressure</a> or <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/questions/everything-else/how-can-storms-affect-my-reception">extreme weather</a> could be causing problems. </p><p>If there is an issue with your local transmitter or you’ve found the answer on a Works & Warnings page, the problem should resolve itself without you doing anything. Consider using <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer">BBC iPlayer</a> or <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds">BBC Sounds</a> while you wait for the issue/work to be resolved. </p><p><br><strong>Step 2 – Check the cabling </strong><br><br>Start by checking the cables that are connected to the television or set-top box and the wall socket. They should be securely connected. If possible, try with another cable, in case the cable or connector is faulty. </p><p><br><strong>Step 3 – Check your television is tuned to the transmitter with the best signal </strong></p><p>You should get the strongest signal from the transmitter your aerial is pointing towards. Some Freeview reception problems are due to the receiver not using the best signal. This can be an issue when signals from more than one transmitter can be received. A manual retune will allow you to choose which transmitter signal to tune to. The Transmitter Checker can help figure out which transmitter your aerial is pointing towards. </p><p>Check our <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview-freely/manual-retuning-to-restore-reception-or-missing-channels">manual retune guide</a> for instructions.  </p><p><br><strong>Step 4 – Check the aerial system </strong></p><p>Next, you might want to consider getting your aerial installation checked. We cannot recommend individual Installers. However <a href="https://www.getmeviewing.org.uk/"><strong>GetMeViewing</strong></a> is the consumer site for CAI Ltd (Confederation of Aerial Industries) which  is a recognised trade body and can put you in touch with one of their members in your area. If you are a tenant or are using a communal aerial, you should contact your landlord/managing agent.  </p><p>Also, please read our guides on: </p><ul><li data-list-item-id="eabb429ed3fa5510440e04b0956ea1a8c"><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview-freely/what-is-a-good-freeview-installation">What is a good Freeview installation </a></li><li data-list-item-id="e3a68d6eaafc24c54cb4e72444037b7e7"><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/everything-else/water-ingress">How to check your cables for water damage </a></li><li data-list-item-id="e8223672d1923125a871d3ffa8b8353ff"><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview/how-to-choose-the-right-amplifier">How to better your signal using an amplifier or attenuator </a></li><li data-list-item-id="e67dafb262459b25289f152afcd9073d8"><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview-freely/who-is-responsible-for-my-sharedcommunal-aerial">Who is responsible for my Shared/Communal Aerial? </a></li></ul><p><br><strong>Other Considerations </strong></p><p>Obstructions between the aerial and transmitter can cause problems. Trees are the most common obstructions. They can affect the signal. This can be greater at different times of the year (when there are more leaves), when wet or in high winds. </p><p>Other examples of obstructions are newly built property nearby, or construction equipment, like a crane. If obstructions are too problematic to overcome and/or permanent, you might want to investigate if you can reposition your aerial and retune to a different transmitter. Another solution would be using another way of receiving services, like <a href="https://www.freesat.co.uk/">Freesat</a> for example. </p><p>If you suspect trees could be a problem, read our guide<a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/questions/freeview-freely/what-is-the-effect-of-trees-on-reception"> What is the effect of trees on reception</a><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/questions/freeview/what-is-the-effect-of-trees-on-reception-1">?</a> </p><p><br><strong>Interference </strong></p><p>If after working though the steps above you are still having problems, it’s possible that interference (an unwanted signal interfering with your reception) could be the cause. Please see our other help site, the <a href="https://www.radioandtvhelp.co.uk/">Radio and Television Investigation Service</a> for further information. </p></blockquote>
</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">How to check your cables for water damage
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<ol>
	<li><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>If possible, check the external cable for any signs of damage, such as cracking and tears. Damaged cables can cause reception problems and can allow water into your installation.</span></span></span></span></span><br />
	 </li>
	<li><span><span><span><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>Find the cable that goes from your aerial or satellite dish into your television, radio or set top box and unplug it. This may be from a socket on the wall or a direct cable through the wall. </span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><br />
	 </li>
	<li><span><span><span><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>If you are using a satellite dish to receive your television, you will also need to check the LNB and cap for any signs of water damage. You may need to instruct a qualified installer to assist you with this.</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><br />
	 </li>
	<li><span><span><span><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>If it is a direct cable, check for any obvious signs of water or a green build-up on the connector. </span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span><span><span><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>If it is from a wall socket check both the connector on the cable and on the wall socket for any signs of water or green build-up.</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> <span><span><span><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>A green build-up is a sign that water has at some point got into your installation. </span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><br />
	 </li>
	<li><span><span><span><span><span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>If you find water damage then it is likely that the cable will need replacing by a qualified aerial installer.</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></li>
</ol>

<p> </p>

<p><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>We cannot recommend individual installers. However the </span></span></span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>CAI (</strong></span></span></span><a href="https://www.getmeviewing.org.uk/"><strong><span lang="EN-US"><span><span><span>Confederation of Aerial Industries</span></span></span></span></strong></a><span lang="EN-US"><span><span><a href="https://www.cai.org.uk/">)</a></span></span></span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span> </span></span></span><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>is a recognised trade body which will be able to put you in touch with one of their members in your area.</span></span></span></p>

<p> </p>
<img alt="External water ingress" data-align="center" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-uuid="b0556763-5cc3-4910-bee9-1ceb7c8b545c" src="/reception/sites/default/files/inline-images/External%20water%20ingress%20%28003%29.jpg" /><img alt="Water ingress screw" data-align="center" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-uuid="a39f3eec-f3cd-4bcb-b2ab-86b1dded55b9" height="483" src="/reception/sites/default/files/inline-images/Water%20ingress%20screw%20on%20v%20compression.png" width="634" />
<p> </p>

</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">How to better my signal using an amplifier or attenuator
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<blockquote>
<hr />
<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>When to use an amplifier</strong> </span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>A signal amplifier should only be used as a last resort when the television signal is weak. Even the best amplifier will still add some noise to the television signal it is amplifying/boosting that could result in picture break up. A good amplifier should have a filter built in that only allows the signal you want to be boosted and not any unwanted signals. Otherwise, all the unwanted signals will also be boosted, which can cause pictures to break up. </span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>Problems using amplifiers</strong> </span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>Amplifiers themselves are a common source of reception problems. For example, if water were to get into a masthead type, they can start to boost the result of the fault. This could be unwanted signals and result in picture loss on your own television and, maybe, those living nearby. To check, remove the power from the amplifier and see whether the problem goes away.</span></span></span></p>

<p> </p>

<p><span lang="EN-US"><span><span>There are three types of amplifier – masthead, set-back and distribution. All these need a power supply to work.</span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>Masthead</strong> </span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>These fit directly under an outside aerial and usually the best type of amplifier to fix weak signals. </span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>Set-back</strong> </span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>These fit between the aerial socket in the wall and your television. </span></span></span></p>

<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>Distribution</strong> </span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>These split the TV signal from a single aerial and allow the signal to be sent to several different televisions in the building.</span></span></span></p>
<img alt="amplifiers" data-caption="Masthead, Set-back and distribution amplifiers" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-uuid="2167962a-473a-4061-b7c6-39be989fe00d" height="295" src="/reception/sites/default/files/inline-images/amps2.jpg" width="524" />
<p> </p>
</blockquote>

<blockquote>
<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>Combined amplifiers</strong> </span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>Some amplifiers are a mix of the above. For example, some masthead amplifiers are also distribution amplifiers. Some can also combine television and FM radio signals. </span></span></span></p>

<p> </p>

<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>Attenuators</strong></span></span></span></em></p>

<p><em><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span><strong>When to use an Attenuator</strong></span></span></span></em></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>If you are experiencing pixellation or picture break up, it may be that your signal is too strong as this often presents itself similarly to a weak signal. This is likely to happen if you live close to a transmitter.</span></span></span></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>Attenuators can be used to decrease the incoming signal if it is too strong without distorting it. It is effectively the opposite of an amplifier, though the two work by different methods. While an amplifier provides gain, boosts the signal, an attenuator provides loss, reduces the signal. Attenuators are always a compromise and should only be used if absolutely necessary.</span></span></span></p>

<p><span lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US"><span><span>They come in a variety of powers; in most cases a small reduction is all that is needed. It may take a little trial and error to find the most suitable one for your installation, and it is worth taking the advice of a local aerial contractor to select the correct one for the installation.</span></span></span></p>
<img alt="Attenuator" data-align="center" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-uuid="df188236-bb2b-4062-bbfc-6ea5a8789d26" src="/reception/sites/default/files/inline-images/Attenuator.jpg" />
<p> </p>
</blockquote>

</div></div><hr>
<div class="initHideChild hideChild hiddencontentblock">
  <span aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="true" class="bttn" onclick="this.parentNode.classList.remove('initHideChild');this.parentNode.classList.toggle('hideChild');">
    <h3 class="gel-great-primer title">Who is responsible for my Shared/Communal Aerial?
    <i class="gelicon gelicon--down"></i></h3>
</span>
<div class="dropdown-menu gel-body-copy" id="works-warning-">
<hr><blockquote><p><span lang="EN-AU">It is worth first checking to see whether the problem is with your own equipment, or the local transmitter. If neighbours are having the same problem it may be that the aerial itself is at fault, or there may be an interfering signal. In either case, you will need to ask your landlord or management committee to solve the problem.</span></p><p> </p><p><em><span lang="EN-AU"><strong>Checking for problems</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Check cables and leads within your property to ensure the problem is not a simple installation fault. Please see our </span><a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/reception/help-guides/freeview-freely/what-is-a-good-freeview-installation"><span lang="EN-US">Freeview Installation guide</span></a><a href="/reception/help-guides/freeview/what-is-a-good-freeview-installation"><span lang="EN-US"> </span></a><span lang="EN-US">for further details. </span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">To see whether there are any faults with the local transmitters use our </span><a href="/reception/check-for-transmitter-faults/"><span lang="EN-US">Transmitter Checker tool.</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> This will help you to see if there are, or have been recently, transmitter faults in your local area. </span></p><p> </p><p><em><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Electrical interference</strong></span></em></p><p><span lang="EN-US">There are differences between a reception problem and one caused by electrical interference. See our </span><a href="/reception/help-guides"><span lang="EN-US">help guides</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> which explain the differences. Our sister site, the </span><a href="https://www.radioandtvhelp.co.uk/"><span lang="EN-US">Radio and Television Investigation Service (RTIS)</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> also has useful information on how to distinguish the difference.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">If it is potentially interference, your landlord or management committee can contact the regulator, Ofcom, for help with solving the problem, </span><a href="https://www.ofcom.org.uk/make-a-complaint/complain-about-wireless-interference/interference-to-tv-and-radio-services"><span lang="EN-US">using their contact web form</span></a><a href="https://www.ofcom.org.uk/complaints/complain-about-wireless-interference/interference-to-wireless-devices-at-home/interference-to-tv-and-radio-services"><span lang="EN-US">.</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> Since it is a communal aerial, you will not be able to contact Ofcom directly.</span></p></blockquote><blockquote><p> </p><p> </p></blockquote>
</div></div><hr>
